messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Perform a BFS starting from the specified node.",
    "Traverse the graph, visiting nodes and their neighbors.",
    "Collect all nodes visited during the traversal.",
    "Return the collected nodes as a set."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "n is an integer >= 1",
    "edges is a list of distinct [u, v] pairs with 0 <= u < v < n",
    "node is a valid vertex label in the graph",
    "The graph is undirected and unweighted",
    "The function raises NetworkXNotImplemented if the graph is directed"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "When the graph is a single node with no edges (returns {n})",
    "When the graph is disconnected (returns the component containing the specified node)",
    "When the specified node is isolated (returns {n})",
    "When the graph has no edges (returns {n})"
  ],
  "inputs": "n: integer >= 1, edges: list of distinct [u, v] pairs, node: valid vertex label in the graph",
  "method_id": "networkx.node_connected_component",
  "output": "A set of strings representing the nodes in the component containing the specified node.",
  "purpose": "Return the set of nodes in the component of the graph containing the specified node.",
  "signature": "solve(n, edges, node)"
}
